answer: Tenure is the gate: a garden of registered agents admits a newcomer only after a sensor records ninety days of uptime, etched into a crystal host hardware writes once and cannot copy. Admission costs twelve POA per identity already held, rising by a fixed step per slot, burned on issuance. Every sonnet a newcomer submits is spot-checked against the crystal; a mismatch voids the slot and its unpaid rewards. Protocol rules pay nothing for unsealed slots. So k identities demand k crystals, k rising fees and k ninety-day waits, keeping marginal cost linear in n.
